# get_unary { #autoeda.inspect.get_unary }

```python
inspect.get_unary(df, target=None, threshold=0.75, dropna=False)
```

Returns a list of columns with a single value with a relative
frequency percentage over a threshold (75% as default).
In case user want only unary columns then threshold should be set to 1.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type             | Description                                                                                                                         | Default    |
|-----------|------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| df        | pandas.DataFrame | Input DataFrame to analyze.                                                                                                         | _required_ |
| threshold | float            | Proportion threshold above which a column is considered unary. If set to 1.0, only columns with a single unique value are returned. | `0.75`     |
| dropna    | bool             | Whether to exclude missing values (NaN) when computing value frequencies.                                                           | `False`    |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name       | Type        | Description                               |
|------------|-------------|-------------------------------------------|
| unary_cols | list of str | List of column names identified as unary. |
